quests.instruction: When r follows a, the vowel sound changes to /ar/. Which word has the /ar/ sound?
quests.hint: Open your mouth wide and growl a little: ar.
quests.explanation: In “farm”, the letters ar make one vowel sound, /ar/. “Fan” has short a and “fame” has long a.
quests.funFact: The letter r is sometimes called a “bossy r” because it changes the sound of the vowel before it.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? c__ — you ride in it.
quests.hint: Think of the vehicle. Which two letters make the sound after /k/?
quests.explanation: “Car” ends with the /ar/ sound spelled ar.

quests.instruction: The word “park” has four letters. How many sounds does it have?
quests.hint: Remember that ar is a single vowel sound.
quests.explanation: “Park” has 3 sounds: /p/ /ar/ /k/. The a and r work together as one sound.
quests.funFact: The letter r changes the vowel before it, so we call these “r-controlled” vowels.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /or/ sound, like “fork”?
quests.hint: Round your lips a little and say or.
quests.explanation: “Corn” has the /or/ sound spelled or. “Can” has short a and “cone” has long o.
quests.funFact: Corn, fork, horse, north and storm all have the /or/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? st__m — dark clouds, rain and thunder.
quests.hint: Say the word for a big weather event. Which vowel sound do you hear?
quests.explanation: “Storm” uses or for the /or/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT have the /or/ sound?
quests.hint: Compare the vowels that have an r after them. Which one is not like the others?
quests.explanation: “Born” and “sort” have /or/. “Barn” has /ar/.

quests.instruction: Which word has /ar/, not /or/?
quests.hint: Open wide for /ar/ and round your lips for /or/.
quests.explanation: “Card” has /ar/. “Cord” has /or/ and “cod” has short o.
quests.funFact: Ar and or look similar, but car has the open /ar/ and corn has the rounder /or/.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same vowel sound as “horse”?
quests.hint: Say horse and feel your lips round for the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Horse” and “north” both have /or/. “Shark” has /ar/ and “nurse” has /er/.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? g__den — you grow flowers there.
quests.hint: Say the word slowly. Which r-controlled vowel do you hear in the first part?
quests.explanation: “Garden” starts with /g/ and /ar/, spelled ar.

quests.instruction: The letters er, ir and ur can make the same sound, as in “fern”. Which word has that sound?
quests.hint: Say fern slowly, then compare the vowel in each choice.
quests.explanation: “Bird” has /er/ spelled ir. “Barn” has /ar/ and “born” has /or/.
quests.funFact: The letters er, ir and ur all make the same sound, so you have to remember which spelling belongs to which word.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? t__n — you do this to a door handle.
quests.hint: Think of what you do with a handle, then decide which vowel sound you hear.
quests.explanation: “Turn” uses ur for the /er/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which word has the ur spelling?
quests.hint: Look for the letters u and r together.
quests.explanation: “Nurse” has ur. “Horse” has or and “shirt” has ir.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? g__l — a young female child.
quests.hint: Say the word. Which r-controlled vowel is in the middle?
quests.explanation: “Girl” uses ir for the /er/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? n__se — a person who helps sick people.
quests.hint: Say the word slowly and think about how it is spelled.
quests.explanation: “Nurse” uses ur. The /er/ sound has three common spellings.

quests.instruction: Which word is spelled with er?
quests.hint: All three words sound the same in the middle. Look at the spelling.
quests.explanation: “Fern” is spelled with er. “Fur” has ur and “fir” has ir.
quests.funFact: Fern, fur and fir sound the same in the middle but are spelled differently.

quests.instruction: Listen to the vowels in these r-controlled words. Which one is different?
quests.hint: Say all three words and listen to the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Bird” and “turn” have /er/. “Star” has /ar/.

quests.instruction: Pick the word with the odd vowel sound out.
quests.hint: One word has a rounder vowel than the other two.
quests.explanation: “Fern” and “girl” have /er/. “Corn” has /or/.

quests.instruction: Which pair of words has the same vowel sound? Look past the spelling.
quests.hint: Say both words and listen to the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Her” and “bird” both have the /er/ sound, spelled er and ir.
quests.funFact: Her, bird and turn all share the same vowel sound, spelled er, ir and ur.

quests.instruction: Which word has a short vowel, not an r-controlled one?
quests.hint: Look for the word where the vowel stands alone with no r after it.
quests.explanation: “Dash” has short a followed by /sh/. In “dart” and “dirt”, the r changes the vowel sound.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /ar/ sound at the beginning?
quests.hint: Say each word. Which one starts with the open /ar/ sound?
quests.explanation: “Arm” starts with /ar/. “Ant” starts with short a and “oar” starts with /or/.
quests.funFact: Arm, art and arch all start with the /ar/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which word has /or/ in the middle and /n/ at the end?
quests.hint: Check both the vowel sound and the last sound.
quests.explanation: “Born” is /b/ /or/ /n/. “Barn” has /ar/ and “burn” has /er/.

quests.instruction: Read the word “first”. Which vowel sound does it have?
quests.hint: Think about the ir spelling you have learned.
quests.explanation: In “first”, ir makes the /er/ sound, followed by /s/ and /t/.
quests.funFact: First, third, girl, shirt and bird all use ir for the /er/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /s/ /p/ /or/ /t/?
quests.hint: Use all four sounds, including the r-controlled vowel.
quests.explanation: /s/ /p/ /or/ /t/ makes “sport”. “Spot” has short o and “spurt” has /er/.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /ch/ /ar/ /t/?
quests.hint: Match each sound, including /ar/ in the middle.
quests.explanation: “Chart” has /ch/ /ar/ /t/. “Chat” is missing the r-controlled sound.

quests.instruction: Which is the correct spelling of the word that means to be on fire?
quests.hint: Think of the spelling for /er/ that you have seen in turn and nurse.
quests.explanation: “Burn” uses ur for /er/. “Bern” and “birn” are not real words.

quests.instruction: Which is the correct spelling for the colour of grape juice?
quests.hint: Think of the first vowel pattern in the word.
quests.explanation: “Purple” starts with ur for the /er/ sound.
quests.funFact: Purple, nurse, turn and burn all use ur for the /er/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which is the correct spelling for the soft covering on a cat?
quests.hint: Two of these are real words. Which one means a cat’s coat?
quests.explanation: “Fur” is the word for an animal’s soft hair. “Fir” is a kind of tree and “fer” is not a word.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same vowel sound as “car”?
quests.hint: Listen for the open /ar/ sound.
quests.explanation: “Car” and “jar” both have /ar/. “Jam” has short a and “jog” has short o.
quests.funFact: Car, jar, star, far and bar all end with the same /ar/ sound.

quests.instruction: Which word has a blend at the start and the /er/ sound?
quests.hint: You need both: two sounds at the start and /er/ in the middle.
quests.explanation: “Skirt” starts with the blend sk and has /er/. “Shark” has /ar/ and “stork” has /or/.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /er/ sound spelled ur?
quests.hint: Find the word with the letters u and r together.
quests.explanation: “Hurt” has ur. “Shirt” has ir and “short” has or.
